pool.text: The first skeleton plan for the location of Kisumu was prepared.
The ship SS William Mackinnon was reassembled and registered in Kisumu.
The railway line from Mombasa reached the Kisumu pier and was named Port Florence.
The township boundaries were gazetted and land set aside for its development.
Winston Churchill visited the growing town of Kisumu during his travels.
A monument was unveiled by the then Governor of Kenya Sir Robert Brooke-Popham.
The town was elevated to the status of a municipal board.
A Lockheed Lodestar aircraft crashed near Kisumu, killing all twelve people on board.
A Douglas C-47 plane crash resulted in twenty-eight fatalities in Kisumu.
The municipality of Kisumu was elevated to the status of a municipal council.
Independence was declared, leading to an influx of locals into the town.
The city's growth and prosperity slowed down due to the community collapse.
Kisumu Museum was established with outdoor pavilions laid out like a Luo homestead.
The area was gazetted as the Ndere Island National Reserve and remained uninhabited.
The city spurred with the reformation of the community and its new designation.
The first aviation incident took place outside Kisumu.
A massive road project for a major overhaul of the network was initiated.
Passenger trains operated between Nairobi and Kisumu using the revamped meter gauge rail.
A song by Zack Okello talks about how Kisumu is growing rapidly.
Some of the events in the story by Andrei Gusev take place in Kisumu.
